name: Sign in with Google
plain: A one click login where Google tells the site who the person is.
meaning: The site gets a signed ID token with sub (stable user ID), email, email_verified, name, picture, locale and for Workspace users the hd domain. Extra scopes can add Calendar, Drive or Contacts. The site gets the same sub every visit.

web.api: Google Identity Services: google.accounts.id.initialize(); OIDC id_token

access.persistence: Google session cookies keep the person signed in; site stores its own session
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings
steps: Person clicks Sign in with Google
Site creates its account or session

limits.headline: Can sign you in with Google and learn your name, email and photo
limits.user_action: You tap Sign in with Google and pick an account in the Google box
can: Receive a Google ID that stays the same each time you visit
Get your name, email, profile photo and language
Learn your company domain when you use a Workspace account
Ask for extra access such as Calendar, Drive or Contacts on a second screen
cannot: See your Calendar, Drive or Contacts unless you approve that extra access
See your email inbox without a separate approval
Sign in without you picking an account

story.what_it_is: A one click login where Google tells the site who you are.

marketing.name: Sign in with Google
marketing.pitch: Google pitches a quick, secure sign in using an account people already have, with one tap on web and mobile.

story.for_you: You click a Google button, pick your account and agree. The site now knows your name, photo and email. Next time it may offer a one tap box right when the page loads.
story.for_makers: Makers skip building password systems and get a verified email. They get a stable user ID and a profile picture for personalizing the app, and sign ups are faster, which improves conversion.

use_cases.example: A web game lets a player sign in with Google so scores, skins and a friends leaderboard follow them to a new laptop.
A cloud gaming service such as GeForce NOW offers account sign in options so a person can start streaming a game on any browser.
An online editor reads the sign in token to open a person's own files and show their picture on live cursors.
A store gets a verified email at checkout, so receipts and order tracking work with no extra form.
A school web app uses the Workspace domain claim to let only students and teachers of that school in.
A growth team counts new accounts made with Google versus email to tune the sign up page.
A site can block throwaway sign ups because Google already checked that the email is real.

risks: Google sees where you sign in
If the Google account is lost, so are the logins

technical_bounds: Default scopes are openid, email and profile
Google also sees every site the person signs in to
Third-party cookie free path via FedCM

abuse: Google learning every site the person uses; email address given to site
